author: Allen Clayton
title: Clarksburg moves to hire outside law firm for internal investigation - NewsBreak
text:
By Allen Clayton ,
1 hours ago
CLARKSBURG, W.Va. (WBOY) — Amid allegations brought against Clarksburg City Manager Tiffany Fell, the Clarksburg City Council met Wednesday evening for a special session to discuss how to handle the situation.
Council members did not publicly discuss any concerns during the brief public portion of the special meeting, which pertained to the potential engagement of legal representation to assist with personnel-related issues. Councilmembers also did not discuss any personnel issues that have been alleged against Fell.
Following the public portion of the special meeting, members entered into a lengthy executive session, which lasted nearly four hours behind closed doors. During that time, the council reviewed confidential information and personnel details not subject to public disclosure under West Virginia’s Open Meetings Law .
“They are just alleged allegations. There is more breadth of, of things that we want looked into besides the allegations and clarification, we’re looking for outside counsel,” Clarksburg Councilman Maring Howe said. “All of council had consensus to retain Spilman, Thomas, & Battle to do that investigation. So, a motion was made to retain them.”
First United Methodist Church meets fundraising goal for Clarksburg Winter Shelter Following the executive session, the special meeting resumed, and Councilman Martin Howe moved that the city obtain legal counsel from law firm Spilman Thomas & Battle to conduct the internal investigation into the city and allegations brought against Fell.
“For us, being just being leaders of the city and being elected officials, we just want to make sure we’re doing the right thing on behalf of the city, the employees, and even for ourselves as we look forward to recommendations,” Howe said. “We wanted somebody unbiased, not included in these conversations, so we have somebody to speak with independently based upon the questions we still have outstanding.”
Regarding any personnel matters or any allegations against Fell, Mayor Jim Malfregeot stated, “no comment” at this time. Earlier this month, the council also went into a nearly three-hour executive session regarding allegations brought against Fell. During that meeting, Vice Mayor Jerry Riffle also stated, “no comment,” regarding the allegations.
Up to this point, 12 News has been unable to obtain specific details regarding the allegations levied against Fell, but earlier this month, the Clarksburg International Association of Fire Fighters Local 89 made a unanimous vote of “no confidence” against Fell, stating that she lacked qualifications regarding her knowledge of firefighter operations.
